title: Captions language can be picked before captions are written
goal: The captions section offers only Add Captions until captions exist, and its language is fixed to US English until then, so someone speaking another language gets wrong captions first and has to switch and transcribe again. The captions mock puts Language above the button, so it is chosen first.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-captions.html ~244-256 (Language and Safe areas above Generate). Code: Sources/Photonz/CaptionsInspector.swift lookBody ~32-39, `else if !editorState.hasCaptions { addCaptionsButton }` hides `language`. The setting defaults to en-US in Sources/Photonz/EditorState+Captions.swift ~94-96. Safe areas row (`guides`) may also belong above, per the mock: decide from the mock and the one-purpose rule, say which in the audit. Keep copy short (UX-PATTERNS section 4).
acceptance: On a video with no captions at Next defaults, the Captions section shows the Language row above Add Captions, as video-captions.html draws it
Picking a language there and pressing Add Captions writes the captions in that language, and the row keeps that choice afterwards
With captions already written the section looks exactly as it does today
A walk opens a video, reads the Language row before Add Captions, and runs green at Next defaults

Audit written under queue/audits/ with a picture of the empty section beside the mock; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Adversarial pass: a first-time user with a non-English recording now sees Language first. Mock draws Language, Guides, Generate (in a state with captions, no empty state drawn), so the empty section shows all three; Add Captions sits in a Generate row like Rewrite does later. Premiere's caption flow also asks the language before transcribing, so this meets what an editor expects.

Verified: new walk captions-language-before-captions-walk (no flags) picks en-GB with the pointer, presses Add Captions at its point, and the new captionsExpectHeardInPickedLanguage check reads that the transcription ran in en-GB; the row still says en-GB after. 9 related walks green. Scripts/test.sh green (12128 tests); one earlier run had a single failure that two reruns did not repeat.

section-fold-motion-walk failed 2 of 3 runs on the 16ms frame budget at different headers (Properties, Transitions, Time), then passed 3 of 3 both with and without this change on a fresh build: the failing runs were the short 36s ones, so it reads as an environment flake, not this change. Left rough here; it did not reproduce enough to file.
left rough: canvas caption badge reads AUTO · EN for every English variant, so en-GB looks like en-US there; a person would rarely notice, not filed. Language stays one app-wide setting (unchanged).
